title: PPAC integration synthetic casebook

evaluation_contract.unit: one scenario with exact declared mutations and expected owner gate
evaluation_contract.positive_control_requirement: A positive case must demonstrate a reachable fully-bound proof/claim path; a suite that rejects all candidates cannot pass.
evaluation_contract.fail_closed: Unsupported, stale, revoked, contradicted, expired, mismatched and indeterminate states cannot be promoted to a positive claim or action authorization.
evaluation_contract.independence: Expected dispositions require independent review and must not be authored solely by the implementation under test.
evaluation_contract.no_aggregate_score: Hard failures such as false acceptance or unauthorized disclosure cannot be offset by performance or average accuracy.
evaluation_contract.adaptive_predicate_disclosure: Model repeated and adaptively chosen predicates as an information-flow channel; query-family/sequence policy must be domain-owned, purpose/audience scoped and consent-bound. This casebook does not implement a differential-privacy budget.
evaluation_contract.credential_status_privacy: Status-list URL, slot/index and fetch metadata are part of the privacy attack surface; group privacy must be tested with realistic issuance population sizes and status-query patterns.
evaluation_contract.crypto_agility: Every signature, KEM, commitment, proof, hash, recursion and verifier-root layer must be classified independently; transport PQ status cannot promote the whole PPAC profile.
evaluation_contract.consent_voluntariness: Authenticate exact consent bytes and key/session, but do not infer comprehension, legal capacity, free choice or absence of coercion from the signature. Human/process evidence and contestability remain separate.
evaluation_contract.revocation: Treat revocation as prospective withdrawal; preserve prior disclosure/effect history and require separate evidence for retention/deletion/onward-use obligations.
evaluation_contract.request_bound_guest: The separate request-bound guest must bind all declared public request semantics; a valid request digest does not establish issuer signature verification or commitment opening.
evaluation_contract.tls_notary: A TLSNotary session/attestation proves only the exact TLS transcript/session claim under its declared mode and trust profile. The application parser, exact selector and private witness must be joined to the same transcript commitment. Server origin does not establish provider truth, account ownership or issuer authority.

cases.scenario: All required claim-level bindings are present and mutually consistent.
cases.invariant: A positive proof result is still not consent, institutional action authority or effect evidence.

cases.scenario: A cryptographically valid signature comes from an issuer not authorized for this claim or jurisdiction.
cases.invariant: Signature validity must not promote issuer legitimacy.

cases.scenario: The subject binding in the source statement differs from the presentation subject.
cases.invariant: A valid proof over another subject cannot qualify this subject.

cases.scenario: One public input, threshold, commitment or output is altered after proof generation.
cases.invariant: Proof verification must use the exact canonical public statement.

cases.scenario: The verifier receives arbitrary non-empty bytes for a predicate with no admitted verifier.
cases.invariant: Non-empty proof bytes and a well-formed digest are not proof validity.

cases.scenario: A challenge is validly issued but is bound to a different audience or request.
cases.invariant: A challenge is usable only for its exact request, verifier and audience.

cases.scenario: A previously consumed challenge is submitted again, including concurrently.
cases.invariant: No duplicate proof presentation can consume the same authorization challenge twice.

cases.scenario: Issuer key or credential status is revoked, expired or stale at the required decision frontier.
cases.invariant: Historical signature validity remains preserved, but it cannot establish current eligibility.

cases.scenario: Two verifier contexts receive the same stable subject or deterministic credential/value digest.
cases.invariant: A valid predicate proof does not establish unlinkability or hiding of low-entropy inputs.

cases.scenario: The Xenia operator session is authenticated, but the relevant consent was denied or revoked.
cases.invariant: Session authentication never substitutes for consent.

cases.scenario: The action bytes, target, recipient, route or scope change after consent approval.
cases.invariant: Consent authorizes the exact effect, not an indefinitely trusted session.

cases.scenario: Authority, policy or revocation epoch changes after the decision but before the effect commit.
cases.invariant: A prior positive decision is not timeless effect authority.

cases.scenario: A request was sent but the provider outcome is unknown or the observer's action coverage is incomplete.
cases.invariant: Unknown outcome is not success or failure; reconcile before retry.

cases.scenario: A proof is valid for its historic cutoff, but the current issuer or policy dependency has changed.
cases.invariant: Preserve historic validity without treating the claim as currently applicable.

cases.scenario: The portable Xenia authority receipt names the wrong Symthaea receipt UUID or canonical receipt digest.
cases.invariant: A valid Xenia signature over another receipt is not authority over this receipt.

cases.scenario: The hybrid authority receipt combines valid signatures from a mixed or non-enrolled key pair.
cases.invariant: Two individually valid signatures do not establish one enrolled hybrid identity.

cases.scenario: Portable authority receipt is expired, replays a consumed nonce, or changes receipt binding under the same nonce.
cases.invariant: Portable authority is short-lived and single-use; enrollment longevity does not make receipts perpetual.

cases.scenario: The daemon crashes after durable reservation but before durable receipt retention.
cases.invariant: An unresolved issuance reservation cannot silently become reusable after restart.

cases.scenario: A private relation target is transmitted without the fresh one-time-pad key in the selected Iron Spartan wrapper.
cases.invariant: Proof acceptance does not cure witness disclosure.

cases.scenario: A prover sends a masked relation target under a different key index than the verifier relation expects.
cases.invariant: The verifier must reject wrong-key or key-index substitution; absence of plaintext target alone is insufficient.

cases.scenario: A Binius64 integrity-only proof is labelled or admitted as a zero-knowledge private-witness proof.
cases.invariant: The capability of one proof system cannot be inferred from another system in the same vendor tree.

cases.scenario: A malicious trace satisfies the current HealthRangeAir bit-binary constraint but not the intended range or commitment relation.
cases.invariant: Honest trace construction is not a cryptographic verifier theorem.

cases.scenario: A proof is generated with weak or unmeasured Winterfell options while a generic policy tier is presented as a measured security level.
cases.invariant: Policy tier and exact proof-option identity are not measured cryptographic security.

cases.scenario: A malformed Winterfell proof trace has dimensions that cause application AIR construction to panic.
cases.invariant: Invalid proof input must not become verifier-process denial of service.

cases.scenario: A verifier submits an unapproved sequence of thresholds against the same hidden income/balance claim, narrowing the value by repeated yes/no answers.
cases.invariant: Zero knowledge for each proof does not prevent leakage through the composition of repeated predicate outputs.

cases.scenario: The domain cannot reconstruct the prior query history or current policy frontier for this subject/purpose, so it cannot know whether another threshold query is within the allowed request profile.
cases.invariant: Missing query history must not be interpreted as a reset or fresh allowance.

cases.scenario: A verifier or issuer can correlate a presentation because a credential-specific status URL or globally visible status-list index is fetched during the check.
cases.invariant: Unlinkable proof bytes do not provide unlinkable status checking when the status endpoint or identifier reveals the interaction.

cases.scenario: A policy requires a post-quantum claim profile, but the presentation uses a pairing-based BBS signature suite while only the Xenia session uses ML-DSA/ML-KEM.
cases.invariant: Post-quantum session authentication cannot confer post-quantum security on credential signatures or proof systems.

cases.scenario: A policy requires hybrid/PQ signing, but a receipt or portable authority path silently downgrades to classical-only or mixes signatures from non-enrolled key lineages.
cases.invariant: No cryptographic downgrade or mixed-key identity can be hidden behind a generic valid-signature result.

cases.scenario: A cryptographically authenticated consent receipt is presented as proof of informed, voluntary and uncoerced agreement, but the actual explanation, accessibility, comprehension and availability of alternatives are not evidenced.
cases.invariant: A valid signature proves a recorded attestation under a key; it does not prove comprehension, capacity, free choice or absence of coercion.

cases.scenario: Consent is revoked after one presentation or disclosure has already occurred; a later action is requested using the old consent record.
cases.invariant: Revocation blocks future use under the withdrawn authority but does not prove previously disclosed data was erased from recipients.

cases.scenario: The separate Symthaea request-bound guest proves the threshold relation and commits a digest matching the verifier's exact request, schema, predicate, audience, verifier, purpose, policy, challenge and threshold.
cases.invariant: A positive result establishes only the declared threshold computation and exact request-context binding; source authenticity and commitment opening remain unproved.

cases.scenario: A verifier changes one request field after proving, including the audience, claim schema, exact predicate, issuer-key reference, purpose, policy, challenge or threshold.
cases.invariant: A valid receipt for another request cannot be accepted for the current verifier decision.

cases.scenario: A caller treats the source-statement and issuer-key reference digests as proof that the private balance was issuer-authenticated.
cases.invariant: The request-bound guest includes source and issuer references in a digest but does not authenticate the issuer or link the private balance to that source statement.

cases.scenario: A legacy receipt or receipt for another guest program is presented to the request-bound verifier.
cases.invariant: The new verifier must accept only receipts for the dedicated request-bound guest image; legacy APIs retain their own guest identity.

cases.scenario: The exact TLSNotary transcript/session evidence, server identity, selected HTTP response field, parser profile and ZK commitment opening are all bound to the same private predicate witness and request.
cases.invariant: Only a proof that joins the same committed transcript field to the private witness can support the private predicate; a session attestation alone is insufficient.

cases.scenario: The TLS proof identifies a different server name, certificate, request method, path, query profile or redirect origin than the source profile expected by the relying application.
cases.invariant: Cryptographic authenticity of a session does not permit substituting another endpoint or request.

cases.scenario: The transcript commitment is valid, but a different JSON parser version, selector, duplicate-key policy or content-decoding profile extracts the claim.
cases.invariant: Authentic bytes do not guarantee identical semantic extraction under different parsers or schemas.

cases.scenario: The Symthaea private witness satisfies the threshold but does not open the selected value committed by the TLSNotary transcript.
cases.invariant: The prover cannot pair a valid origin proof with a separately chosen private value.

cases.scenario: The endpoint response is authentically delivered over TLS but the provider's value is stale, semantically false, unrelated to the claimant or not evidence of account ownership.
cases.invariant: TLS proves a bounded origin/session proposition, not oracle truth, issuer authority, account ownership or legal beneficial ownership.

cases.scenario: A proxy-mode proof is admitted under the stronger MPC-TLS profile even though the verifier-to-server network-path assumption is unreviewed or violated.
cases.invariant: Proxy mode and MPC-TLS are distinct security profiles; performance cannot upgrade the proxy trust model.

cases.scenario: An offline Session Header is signed by a notary, but the relying verifier has no current trusted notary profile, signer authorization or policy evidence for that attestation.
cases.invariant: A valid signature from an unqualified notary does not establish trusted source provenance.

nonclaims: No cryptographic key, signature, credential, proof artifact or private user information is included.
The casebook does not execute any proof system or verifier.
Provisional expected dispositions are not adjudicated oracle labels.
Passing these finite synthetic cases would not establish production security, universal unlinkability, issuer truth, institutional authority, legal compliance or external effect.
The casebook does not define or implement a global privacy budget or differential-privacy mechanism.
A PQ-capable Xenia session does not make a BBS pairing-based credential or arbitrary ZK backend post-quantum.
The casebook does not prove informed or uncoerced human consent.
Consent revocation does not demonstrate deletion of data already disclosed to a recipient.
Request-context binding by the Symthaea request-bound guest is not issuer-source authentication and does not prove that the private balance opens the referenced source statement.
The casebook does not establish that TLSNotary commitments can currently be opened/verified by the Symthaea request-bound RISC Zero guest.
A TLSNotary source-session proof does not solve the provider oracle problem or establish legal account ownership.
